event.canonical_title: New Restraining Order Filed Against GOP Rep. Max Miller Amid Abuse Allegations
event.summary: The daughter of a senator has filed a new restraining order against GOP Representative Max Miller, who is facing domestic abuse allegations. event_overview.title: About New Restraining Order Filed Against GOP Rep. Max Miller Amid Abuse Allegations
event_overview.subject: New Restraining Order Filed Against GOP Rep. Max Miller Amid Abuse Allegations
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a public and legal dispute involving Rep. Max Miller, an Ohio Republican, and his former wife, Emily Moreno, over domestic-abuse allegations, child-custody litigation, and related civil claims. Miller has denied abusing Moreno or their child and has separately sued Moreno and her lawyers for defamation; the allegations had also prompted a House Ethics Committee investigation as of August 5, 2026.

facts.label: People and office
facts.value: Max L. Miller is the Republican U.S. representative for Ohio’s 7th Congressional District; Emily Moreno is his former spouse and the daughter of Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno.

facts.label: Underlying litigation
facts.value: The dispute has unfolded alongside litigation over custody of Miller and Moreno’s minor child. On May 13, 2026, Miller filed a Cuyahoga County civil defamation case against Moreno and her attorneys, alleging that abuse accusations were false and damaging; the filing identifies the case as CV 26 138810 and seeks damages exceeding $25,000.

facts.label: Relevant Ohio legal framework
facts.value: Ohio Revised Code §3113.31 permits domestic-violence civil-protection-order petitions by qualifying family, household, or dating-relationship parties. It allows same-day ex parte hearings when requested and permits temporary restrictions or other relief when the court finds good cause, but proceedings do not replace other civil or criminal remedies.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-July to August 5, 2026 escalation—an attorney-contact restraining-order request, Bernie Moreno’s public criticism, and House Ethics action—but does not resolve the underlying allegations, custody proceedings, or defamation case.
